No. There is no minimum age. Early use of pictures, gestures and speech together supports development.
About 25 words make up most of a toddler's talk, and about 200 core words cover most everyday speech. Keeping them in fixed places builds motor memory.
Why so few pictures of things?
Families whose device did not work in their home language used it far less. Use every language your family speaks.
Should we only use the school language?
Children learn to use a communication app by seeing adults use it. Tap the words while you talk, every day, without asking the child to copy.
How will my child learn it?
No test of readiness is needed. A communication app works best when adults keep it simple, always available, and use it themselves.
Does my child need to be "ready" first?
No. Research shows that communication tools like this app don't hold back speech, and may even help. They're a bridge to talking, not a replacement.
Will this stop my child from learning to talk?
